subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or preserve logged fallback after live OAuth-inheritance proof?
rationale: This choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context can silently cross provider boundaries after auth loss, and repository policy treats auth/provider routing and fallback behavior as security- and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and fail-closed or visible-warning policy
options.body: Keep the issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define operator-visible behavior when auth-route loss would trigger fallback.

options.title: Split visibility after OAuth proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation part after live proof and track fallback warning or fail-closed behavior in a narrower canonical issue.

options.title: Accept logged fallback
options.body: Keep the current log-level fallback behavior after source and live proof, explicitly accepting the operator-surprise and privacy tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and fail-closed or visible-warning policy
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define operator-visible behavior when auth-route loss would trigger fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and nearby history point to this handle for the cross-surface auth, Codex bridge, and subagent routing policy decision.
